extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, agency counsel, and NEPA compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for agencies implementing NEPA procedures, specifically adoption and application of other agencies' categorical exclusions (CEs), preparation and handling of Environmental Assessments (EAs) and Findings of No Significant Impact (FONSIs), and lead agency roles. Focuses on procedural steps, transparency, documentation, supplementation, and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary circumstances assessment when applying an adopted CE
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of extraordinary circumstances occurs at the stage of application and evaluation of a particular action (not at adoption) to determine whether the particular action normally covered by a CE requires preparation of an EA or EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ swaps proposed paragraphs to place extraordinary circumstances at application stage; removed reference to a 'category of proposed actions.' Agencies should evaluate extraordinary circumstances when applying the adopted CE to the specific proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain process for evaluating extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting agencies must explain the process the agency will use to evaluate for extraordinary circumstances when adopting another agency's CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies consult regarding appropriateness of the CE, they should discuss how the adopting agency will review for extraordinary circumstances (e.g., whether the adopting agency will apply the establishing agency's extraordinary circumstances exclusively or both agencies' provisions). The adopting agency should explain how it will address extraordinary circumstances in its notification. CEQ expects agencies to follow the extraordinary circumstances process set forth in the NEPA procedures containing the CE but may also consider their own procedures if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification of CE adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must provide public notification when they adopt another agency's CE for a proposed action or category of actions, consistent with section 109(3) of NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term 'public notification' (not 'public notice') and the phrase 'is adopting' to clarify notice is about adoption. The notice must include a brief description of the proposed action or category of proposed actions 'to which the agency intends to apply the adopted categorical exclusion' and must specify the process for consideration of extraordinary circumstances. The notice must also include a brief description of the consultation process required by §1501.4(c)(2) to demonstrate that consultation occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statutory requirement to seek public comment on adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute does not require agencies to solicit public comment on adoption of another agency's CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declines to add a mandatory requirement to seek comment on adoption; CEQ encourages agencies to seek comment in appropriate cases (e.g., community interest) but does not impose a statutory obligation to seek formal public comments or agency responses for the adoption notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and publication of each application of an adopted CE
rubrics_metrics.description: When an adopting agency applies an adopted CE to a specific proposed action, it must prepare and publish documentation of that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (e)(5) requires agencies to publish the determination that application of the CE is appropriate and that there are no extraordinary circumstances requiring preparation of an EA or EIS, including the analysis required by §1501.4(b)(1) if the agency determines no potential for significant effects notwithstanding extraordinary circumstances. Use of the defined term 'publish' provides agencies discretion on the appropriate manner to publish and does not require disclosure of pre-decisional or deliberative materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated adoption notice permitted; application-specific documentation still required
rubrics_metrics.description: An adopting agency may publish a single notice of adoption when adopting one or more CEs for one or more categories of actions, but must document each subsequent specific application of the adopted CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single adoption notice satisfies section 109(3) for adoption; however, section 109(4) requires documentation of each application of the CE to particular proposed actions, and agencies must publish that documentation to provide transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot modify the text of an adopted CE
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency adopting another agency's CE must adopt the CE 'as established' and may not modify the text of the adopted CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may describe a narrower set of actions in the public notification for which they intend to apply the adopted CE; if they wish to narrow or otherwise modify the CE text, they should instead substantiate and establish a new CE in their agency NEPA procedures. If an agency later seeks to apply the adopted CE to a different category than identified in the adoption notice, it must consult with the establishing agency and provide new public notification consistent with §1501.4(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: EA contents: purpose and need, alternatives, and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: An Environmental Assessment must briefly discuss the purpose and need for the proposed action, alternatives (including reasonable alternatives and the no action alternative), and environmental effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ restructures §1501.5(c)(2) into subparagraphs (i)-(iii) to improve readability and list requirements clearly. For proposals involving unresolved conflicts over resource use (section 102(2)(H)), analysis of reasonable alternatives will generally be required in addition to the proposed and no action alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA must list agencies and persons consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: Each EA must list the agencies and persons consulted in the development of the EA, and 'agencies' includes Federal agencies and State, Tribal, and local governments and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is moved into its own paragraph (§1501.5(c)(3)) to clarify who should be listed and improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA must include a unique identification number for tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Each EA must include a unique identification number that can be used for tracking the EA and carried forward to other related documents (including the FONSI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must also use these identification numbers in any agency databases or tracking systems. CEQ will provide instructions (e.g., numbering format or assignment) following issuance of the final rule; agencies retain some discretion pending CEQ guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft EA public comment invitation when published
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency chooses to publish a draft EA, it must invite public comment on the draft and consider those comments when preparing a final EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ includes paragraph (e) as proposed to codify that inviting comment is required when a draft EA is published. CEQ declines to mandate that all EAs be published for comment; agencies retain discretion on whether to publish draft EAs. CEQ also declines to require agencies to respond to comments or publish comments on a website, leaving such decisions to agency discretion to avoid deterrence from publishing drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA page limits and senior official approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision to page limit procedures to align with section 107(e)(2) of NEPA, dispensing with the requirement for senior agency official approval to exceed 75 pages (not including citations or appendices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ makes this change consistent with statutory provisions; no commenters opposed this change and it is made in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation and reevaluation of EAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should supplement EAs when changes to a proposed action or new information indicate potential for significant effects and when an action is incomplete or ongoing; agencies may use reevaluation to document that supplementation is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §1501.5(h) aligns EA supplementation standards with §1502.9 for EISs. CEQ uses 'should' (not 'may') to indicate supplementation is appropriate where new circumstances or information indicate potential significant effects and the action remains incomplete or ongoing. §1501.5(h)(2) also allows agencies to prepare supplements when doing so furthers NEPA's purposes. §1501.5(i) permits a short reevaluation memo describing why changes do not warrant supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of EIS provisions to EAs (generally should/may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies generally should apply provisions regarding incomplete or unavailable information (e.g., §1502.21) to EAs and may apply other provisions from parts 1502 and 1503 as appropriate to improve EA efficiency and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retains 'generally should' for §1502.21 to acknowledge limited circumstances where it may not apply. CEQ encourages agencies to apply other parts (e.g., scoping §1502.4, cost-benefit §1502.22, environmental review and consultation §1502.24, response to comments §1503.4) where useful, leaving discretion to agency judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and basis for preparing a FONSI
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency prepares a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) after completing an EA when it determines NEPA does not require preparation of an EIS because the proposed action will not have significant effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule subdivides paragraph (a) to clarify sequence: FONSI follows EA; a mitigated FONSI is also based on the EA; if the agency determines the action will have significant effects, it must prepare an EIS following the EA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mitigated FONSIs and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may issue a mitigated FONSI when mitigation is incorporated into the action to reduce effects below significance, but agencies must have a reasonable basis to conclude mitigation will occur and be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ stresses mitigated FONSIs cannot be based on net-benefit tradeoffs across different resource effects; each type of effect must be considered separately. The mitigated FONSI must state enforceable mitigation requirements or commitments and the authority to enforce them (examples include permit conditions, agreements, incidental take statements, terms and conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation monitoring and compliance plan when EA relies on mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an EA relies on mitigation as part of the action to reach a FONSI, the agency must prepare a mitigation and compliance plan for the enforceable mitigation and any other mitigation required by §1505.3(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures agencies take steps to ensure assumed mitigation will occur and be effective, consistent with NEPA purposes and safeguarding the integrity of environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency supervision for multi-agency EAs/EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: A lead agency must supervise the preparation of any EIS or EA for an action or group of actions involving more than one Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ removed the undefined term 'complex EAs' and relies on the existing text describing situations where more than one Federal agency participates; the lead agency responsibility applies broadly where multiple Federal agencies are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint lead agency invitation and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal, State, Tribal, or local agencies may serve as a joint lead agency upon invitation from the Federal lead agency and acceptance by the invited agency; joint lead agencies must fulfill the role of a lead agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies Federal agencies are retained as potential joint leads in some circumstances for efficiency. CEQ revises paragraph (b) for consistency and uses singular 'agency' in the first sentence but does not intend to be overly restrictive; generally only one joint lead agency is anticipated but multiple are not categorically precluded.
